`Some(true)` = limit-TP (`tpOrdKind=limit`), `Some(false)` = trigger-TP
(`tpOrdKind=condition`). This is the single source of truth carried IN the
config so every `dispatchTpslConfig` call site forwards it — no consumer

with trigger+limit-order, since both carry a non-empty order price).

(spot/margin) unchanged; only the contract OCO confirm sets it explicitly.

derivation (behavior unchanged for spot/margin).

name: refresh_margin_context
doc:
Re-derive the full margin context from the Rust trade core + the current
instrument snapshot. Replaces the Kotlin `pushMarginV1ContextToRust`
bridge (B1): the host no longer reads OKTradeCore (`getMarginModeManager`
/ `TradeCommonUtils.isCross` / `BizInstrument.level` / `MarginSwitchView`)
and pushes the result — it only *signals* that the context may have
changed (instrument change / margin-mode toggle), and Rust does every
derivation here:
* account flags ← `derive_margin_account_flags` (V1
`TradeCommonUtils.isMultipleAccount` / `isAutoBorrow`)
* td_mode + is_cross ← `derive_margin_td_mode` (V1
`MarginModeManager.getCurrentMarginMode`), keyed by the current
instrument family (margin/spot: inst_family == inst_id)
* leverage ← the session instrument snapshot's `lever` (V1 pushed
`BizInstrument.level`; the snapshot already carries it). max_leverage
mirrors current until the async max-lever fetch lands — same as the
V1 bridge.

Mirrors V1's two trigger points (instrument observer + MarginSwitchView
`.marginSwitchMode` observer) which both re-ran `pushMarginV1ContextToRust`.
`is_margin_switch_open` is intentionally NOT set here: no margin-pure
derivation reads it, so the dead push is dropped (it keeps its default).

name: apply_instrument_selection
doc:
Record an AUTHORITATIVE instrument selection established OUTSIDE the sheet —
a route seed (the K-line buy/sell-marker jump) or the "current pair" switch.

The entry chip has to read exactly like the sheet row it stands for, so the
label is derived here with the SAME rule the browse rows use
(`filter_row_title_for`) instead of being re-derived by the host. Independent
of `load_filter_data`, so it is valid before the entries list has ever been
built — which is the point: a route seed is known at page open, long before
anyone opens the sheet.

An empty `inst_id` means there is no instrument filter at all and CLEARS the
selection — that is exactly what the chip's "All Instrument" label stands for.

A pair that IS named but cannot be titled here LEAVES the committed selection
untouched, because "I cannot name this" is not "there is no filter" and clearing
would silently drop a selection the sheet legitimately made. That covers an
unknown line, an instrument the biz layer has not loaded yet, and EVENTS —
deliberately not handled, since its filter rows are event SERIES, not
instruments, so labelling one as an instrument would misreport the row it
corresponds to.
